name: Installation scheduling support
short: Organize approved installation dates, access notes, and preparation records for your installation manager.
tasks: Confirm customer access and preparation instructions
Track materials-ready status supplied by your team
Record schedule changes and unresolved dependencies
heroAlt: Field professional reviewing a clipboard at a work site

roleFit: This lane fits HVAC installation managers coordinating approved jobs while retaining authority over crew capacity, scope, safety, and date changes.
Start when each installation has a named lead, an approved calendar entry, and a documented readiness checklist for customer access and prerequisites.
problem: Access instructions, customer availability, permit status, and materials-ready updates can arrive in separate records. Without a shared installation queue, the manager has to reconstruct readiness from messages.
Installation coordination keeps each administrative dependency attached to the work order and identifies the person who must resolve it before the next approved step.
inputsAccess: Provide the installation work order, approved calendar, manager-reviewed date, site contact, customer access notes, readiness checklist, and permit or materials status from the authorized owner.
Use role-based calendar and work-order access, approved preparation messages, and a named installation manager for date conflicts, missing approvals, and readiness exceptions.
workflowSteps: Match each installation request to its approved work order, installation lead, and current calendar entry.
Check the readiness fields for site access, customer preparation, permit status, and material readiness against the named source for each field.
Send only the approved customer access or preparation notice and record its date, channel, and source template.
Record schedule or readiness updates supplied by authorized owners without changing crew assignments or treating a requested date as confirmed.
Route conflicting dates, missing prerequisites, and unconfirmed dependencies to the installation manager with the affected job record.
Close the shift with each open installation, its next action, source time, and named owner visible in the handoff.
deliverables: An installation readiness queue keyed by work-order ID, showing the approved date, access status, prerequisites, source time, and next owner.
A manager exception summary for missing permits, materials updates, customer access details, or schedule approval.
qualityControls: Match every installation calendar change to a dated instruction from the authorized installation manager and preserve the previous approved date in the record history.
Before handoff, confirm each readiness status has a named source and timestamp; leave unknown permit or materials states open instead of inferring completion.
exceptionPaths: Route conflicting installation dates, missing scope approvals, permit questions, customer complaints, and material delays to the named installation manager.
Send urgent site safety reports through the company's emergency procedure; do not leave them in the routine installation scheduling queue.
decisionBoundaries: The assistant may update installation records from approved sources and send approved preparation messages, but cannot confirm unapproved dates, assign crews, certify readiness, interpret permits, or direct field work.
Installation design, equipment selection, technical scope, safety, contract terms, price, and customer commitments remain with qualified or authorized staff.
startingScenarios: Start with one service area's approved installation calendar for a week; reconcile access details and materials status while the installation manager approves every date change.
Pilot the readiness checklist on a small set of scheduled installations and return missing permit or material evidence to its source owner before marking a prerequisite complete.

faqs.q: Can installation scheduling support confirm a new customer date?
faqs.a: It can record a requested date and prepare the calendar update, but only the installation manager can confirm capacity and approve the revised date.

faqs.q: Who verifies that materials are ready for an installation?
faqs.a: The assistant records the materials-ready status supplied by the designated operations or warehouse owner and routes a missing confirmation to that owner.

faqs.q: Can the assistant decide that an installation is ready to proceed?
faqs.a: No. The assistant checks the documented readiness fields and shows missing evidence; the authorized installation lead makes the readiness decision.

name: Service agreement administration
short: Keep agreement records, approved document versions, and customer handoffs organized.
tasks: Index signed agreements supplied by authorized staff
Check administrative fields against the approved checklist
Track missing signatures and document versions
Route scope and coverage questions to the agreement owner

roleFit: This lane fits HVAC service managers or contract administrators who maintain executed service agreements, approved amendments, and renewal records in a named system of record.
Start with one agreement type where the contract owner has documented which fields may be checked administratively and which terms require interpretation.
problem: Signed service agreements, addenda, equipment schedules, and renewal dates can be stored in different places, making it difficult to identify the current approved version for a customer or site.
Agreement administration creates a version-linked record and routes missing signatures, changed scope, and customer term questions to the named agreement owner.
inputsAccess: Provide executed agreements and amendments, customer and site identifiers, approved agreement templates, effective and renewal dates, the agreement repository, and the administrative field checklist.
Grant role-based access to the approved records and customer contact templates; name the contract owner for scope, coverage, pricing, cancellation, and retention decisions.
workflowSteps: Confirm the customer, service location, agreement identifier, and authorized source before opening an agreement record.
Index the signed agreement and each approved amendment as separate, dated versions; do not replace the prior agreement file.
Check administrative fields such as signatures, identifiers, document date, and listed site against the approved checklist.
Add owner-approved effective, renewal, and notice dates to the agreement register and place upcoming actions in the review queue.
Send only approved receipt or renewal communications, record the source version and contact attempt, and route term questions to the agreement owner.
Hand off missing signatures, conflicting versions, and unreviewed scope changes with the next action and named contract owner.
deliverables: A version-linked agreement register with customer, service site, signed document, approved amendments, effective date, renewal date, and owner.
A renewal and documentation queue showing missing signatures, pending amendments, upcoming owner review, and customer questions.
qualityControls: Reconcile every agreement-register change to the signed source or an amendment approved by the named contract owner; retain the prior version and date.
Sample records for matching customer and site identifiers, signature status, version ordering, and renewal dates before a reminder is sent.
exceptionPaths: Pause an agreement update when signed versions conflict, a required signature is missing, a listed site or unit differs, or a customer disputes the recorded term.
Route scope, coverage, price, cancellation, renewal exception, and legal interpretation questions to the authorized agreement owner or qualified adviser.
decisionBoundaries: The assistant may index signed agreements, check listed administrative fields, and send approved notices; it may not interpret coverage, modify contract terms, approve an amendment, or promise a renewal outcome.
Contract scope, equipment coverage, pricing, credit, cancellation, legal interpretation, and customer commitments remain with the authorized agreement owner or qualified professional.
startingScenarios: Start by indexing signed service agreements for one service area, linking each current version and approved amendment to its customer and site record.
Pilot the upcoming renewal queue for one month; prepare approved reminders and route every disputed term or missing signature to the contract owner.

faqs.q: Can the assistant decide whether a repair is covered by an agreement?
faqs.a: No. The assistant can retrieve the signed agreement and log the question, while the authorized agreement owner determines how its terms apply.

faqs.q: How are amendments kept separate from the original agreement?
faqs.a: Each signed amendment is indexed as its own dated version and linked to the agreement; the prior file remains available for review.

faqs.q: Who approves a renewal reminder or agreement change?
faqs.a: The agreement owner approves the applicable term and any change; support sends only the approved reminder or records the signed change.
